best_for: Developers, support agents and writers who type the same replies and snippets all day and are happy to keep them in a text file.

points.title: Type a short code, get the full text
points.text: You set a trigger such as `:br` and Espanso swaps it for a longer reply in any app as you type. Saved keystrokes add up when you send the same answers dozens of times a day.

points.title: Snippets live in YAML files
points.text: Matches go in `match/base.yml` inside the Espanso config folder, and the app reloads as soon as you save. `espanso edit` opens the file for you. There is no settings window yet, so expect to edit text by hand.

points.title: Can run scripts and fill forms
points.text: A snippet can run a shell command or script and paste its output, or show a small form and use your answers. Alt+Space opens a search bar for snippets you cannot remember. More packages come from the Espanso Hub.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Espanso is GPL-3.0 and asks only for optional donations. There is no account and no cloud; your snippets stay in files on your computer, which also makes them easy to back up or keep in Git.

points.title: The Mac catch: Secure Input
points.text: macOS blocks text expansion in password fields. If an app, often a password manager, leaves Secure Input switched on, Espanso stops working everywhere until it is released. The menu bar icon changes to warn you.

points.title: Windows is x64 only
points.text: Windows needs version 10 or later on x64; Arm support is only planned. The installer sets it up for the current user, and SmartScreen may warn you the first time. The Windows listing keeps 11 versions. The Mac build is universal for macOS 10.13 or later, and only the current release is listed.
